text:
alex: quick question — for SDKs (py/ts/go) should we standardize on a single iterator abstraction that sits above multiple transport modes (http/stream/grpc) or let each language pick the best ergonomic surface?
priya: i'm leaning single abstraction. less cognitive load for users. but we need a thin transport adapter surface so languages can map idioms.
jamie: agree w/ priya. single iterator + transport adapters. main tradeoff: how much behavior to bake into iterator (retries, resume) vs adapter.
rachel: +1. we should also decide where idempotency lives. if iterator retries, it needs resume tokens / opaque cursors returned by server.
alex: good point. proposal: iterator core handles user ergonomics (sync/async, next page) and exposes hooks for these concerns: - `adapter.fetch(window, resume_token?)` - `adapter.resume_policy` - `adapter.stream_mode`
priya: can we sketch a tiny example?
jamie: sure — pseudo:
```
// SDK iterator core (language-agnostic)
while (it.next()) {
  batch = adapter.fetch(it.window, it.resume)
  it.emit(batch.items)
  it.update_resume(batch.resume_token)
}
```
adapter.fetch could be implemented over grpc streaming, http/paged, or http/streaming-multipart.
rachel: and for retries, adapter.fetch should return structured error codes and whether the server preserved resume token semantics. server can respond with `retryable: true/false` and `fresh_resume` field.
alex: we should define a small negotiation header so client and server agree on resume semantics and multiplexing. e.g. `X-RW-Resume: v1;mode=opaque;multiplex=true`
jamie: multiplexing is the scary bit — means a single connection may carry multiple logical cursors. good for latency but increases complexity for adapters. we should make multiplex optional and gated behind capability negotiation.
priya: language ergonomics: python iterator should feel like a generator, ts should give async iterable, go should give channel/iterator. core API stays the same, adapters provide impl.
rachel: what about backoff strategies? per-request exponential backoff vs window-level backoff?
alex: recommend default window-level backoff: when a fetch for a window fails transiently, backoff and retry that window. if resume token invalid -> fallback to page-keyed resume (if available) or surface error.
jamie: also add a small idempotency token header `X-RW-Idempotency: <nonce>` for each fetch so server can dedupe.
priya: telemetry: we must emit metrics at adapter boundary: fetch_latency, retry_count, resume_mismatch, multiplex_failures.
rachel: ops: can we log a short example of response shape so adapters can parse resume token safely?
jamie: example response JSON:
```
{
  "items": [...],
  "resume_token": "base64-opaque",
  "cursor_kind": "opaque|page|stream_offset",
  "retryable": true
}
```

sre-bot: FYI — RFC draft link posted: https://r.rw/sdks/iter-transport (automated) :link:
alex: action items: 1) define adapter interface minimal surface (fetch, close, capabilities) 2) draft negotiation headers + response shape 3) add telemetry hooks 4) prototype python generator + http/paged adapter  — volunteering: i'll do (4) this sprint.
priya: i'll author the adapter interface PR and unit tests.
jamie: i'll prototype multiplex header parsing in go adapter.
rachel: i'll write ops playbook for resume mismatch incidents.
alex: sweet. if no objections i'll turn this into a short RFC + example impl next week. :thumbsup:
